title: Can Regenerative Agriculture Really Heal Humans And The Planet?
summary: Podcast page promoting Rodale Institute claims that regenerative organic farming matches conventional yields, earns farmers more and produces more nutritious food.

assertions.quote: organic agriculture leads to equal or better yields than conventional (sometimes over 30% better)
Opponents say it can’t be scaled to the level we need to feed our current and growing population, but the real data actually says otherwise.
three to six times more profits for the farmer

verdicts.note: A global meta-analysis found organic farms 22 to 35 percent more profitable when price premiums are paid, far below several-fold claims, and not without premiums.
ERS cites McBride et al. (2015) finding higher economic returns for organic field crops, mainly from the price premium; this is a secondary citation covering field crops only.

A meta-analysis of 44 studies (55 crops, 14 countries, 40 years) found organic agriculture 22-35% more profitable (net present value) than conventional once actual price premiums were applied, but 23-27% less profitable without them, so the advantage rests on the premium; the studies are largely field trials without subsidies or externalities.

assertions.quote: organic carrots had dramatically higher levels of phytonutrients
healthy soil = healthy food = healthy people

verdicts.note: Soil health gains are measurable, but evidence linking organic soil management to better human health outcomes is lacking.

assertions.quote: Evolving beyond the current organic standard with the launch of the Regenerative Organic Certification
